subject: Consumption fidelity & scale pathway — renewal options
summary: Renewal discussion focused on balancing rising token consumption with predictable performance. Customer requests pricing and term options for a dedicated pool to handle peak-hour latency; sales proposes a stepped committed capacity add-on and a 12-month amendment with churn protection and unit-price discounts. Technical notes address KV cache hit rates and batching opportunities. Procurement/legal next steps outlined.
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@cloudstore.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Q3 consumption snapshot + renewal planning

Hi Anna —

Hope you're well. I pulled a short consumption snapshot for CloudStore's Q3 usage and attached the CSV (Q3-2026_consumption_breakdown.csv). Two quick observations: overall token spend is +48% QoQ, and there's a clear peak in the 11:00–14:00 PST window where tail-latency increases and KV cache misses rise.

Given the upcoming renewal window in December, I'd like to align on whether CloudStore prefers to:
- keep on-hosted usage and add surge headroom credits, or
- move a portion of the workload to a Dedicated pool for predictable latency during peaks.

If you’re open, can we schedule 30 minutes next week to walk the consumption graph and talk through a pricing/term option for a hybrid setup? Naomi (CS lead) is looped for ops context.

Thanks —
Marcus
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q3-2026_consumption_breakdown.csv
From: Anna Li <anna@cloudstore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@cloudstore.com
Date: 2026-11-02T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Q3 consumption snapshot + renewal planning

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. Two reactions from our side:
1) The latency spikes during the noon window are causing user complaints for our chat assist feature; we have a remediation task but long-term we need something more predictable.
2) We will likely expand usage into a new recommendation microservice next quarter, which will increase steady-state tokens.

Before a meeting, can you provide a back-of-envelope for:
- a dedicated pool sized for our current peaks (est. 4x baseline concurrency) including monthly committed price and per-token overage, and
- the ROI case vs. staying hosted with surge credits (we have to justify this to our finance team).

I put contracts on CC so they see timing. We can do a call Wednesday (11/4) at 10am PT.

— Anna
Director, Platform Engineering
CloudStore
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@cloudstore.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T07:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 consumption snapshot + renewal planning

Appreciate the context, Anna —

I've sketched two immediate options (see brief bullets below). I'll bring Ben (SRE/SE) on the call to run through technical tradeoffs and Naomi to speak to SLA/operational support.

Option A — Hosted + surge credits:
- No infra change.
- Add monthly surge credits equivalent to ~25% of current Q3 spend to absorb peaks.
- Lower up-front cost, higher variable spend; latency variability remains possible.

Option B — Dedicated pool (recommended for predictable latencies):
- Initial reserved capacity to cover observed peak concurrency window (estimated 10 GPUs equivalent) + autoscale headroom for bursts.
- Pricing: committed monthly fee + per-token rate on overage. Back-of-envelope: committed fee ~$48k/month with overage at hosted unit price minus 10% (detailed calc on call).
- Includes 99.9% P95 latency SLO during peak lanes and higher telemetry retention.

We'll prepare a short ROI slide for the call comparing expected user-impact cost of latency (support tickets, conversions) vs. incremental committed cost. Meeting confirmed for 11/04 10:00am PT.

—Marcus

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 10:00 AM Anna Li <anna@cloudstore.com> wrote:
> Confirming call — joining from the Bay.
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Anna Li <anna@cloudstore.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T13:25:00-08:00
Subject: Technical note: tail latency drivers + caching levers

Anna — great to chat earlier. A few technical notes from the troubleshooting thread and the quick perf run we did during the call: 
- The dominant driver of the noon tail is KV cache churn for long-context batched requests; cache hit rate drops ~18% in the 11–13 window.
- Recommending two parallel mitigations: increase dedicated GPU headroom for the slot, and enable a conservative prefix cache on the recommendation microservice (can be toggled client-side).
- Expected outcome: p95 latency reduction from ~850ms -> ~200–300ms for peak workloads when we move to Dedicated and enable prefix caching.

I'll attach the latency trace PDF and a short runbook for the prefix cache toggle. If CloudStore wants, we can validate in a 48-hour pilot on a small portion of traffic.

Attachments: peak-latency-traces-2026-10.pdf

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@cloudstore.com>, contracts@cloudstore.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed amendment & commercial outline (draft)

Anna / Contracts —

Following up with a draft amendment and a commercial outline attached (redwood-dedicated-amendment-v1-redline.docx). High-level:
- 12-month committed term for a Dedicated pool sized to cover current peaks; tiered discounts (month 1–3 at list, 10% discount months 4–12 provided we reach a minimum monthly usage threshold).
- Option to convert to a blended committed contract for year 2.
- Startup credit: two weeks of free burst capacity during onboarding and prefix-cache tuning.

Financial back-of-envelope included in the doc. If legal is comfortable with the amendment language we can route for a signature and plan a 48-hour pilot window for perf validation.

Please review and let me know any redlines — happy to jump in with legal.

Best,
Marcus

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-amendment-v1-redline.docx
From: Anna Li <anna@cloudstore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@cloudstore.com, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed amendment & commercial outline (draft)

Thanks Marcus — I reviewed the amendment with our procurement team and a few comments from contracts: minimal changes to SLA wording, confirm the 10% conditional discount triggers, and add a procurement-friendly cancellation clause (30-day notice after the initial 90-day onboarding).

Overall we like the Dedicated approach and the pilot. Next steps for us:
- Contracts to send a redlined version by 11/12;
- Procurement to run internal finance sign-off week of 11/15;
- We expect to start the 48-hour pilot during the week of 11/22 if approvals go smoothly.

Anna
Director, Platform Engineering
CloudStore
